gitCommit.subject: Batch the backfill, and unbomb two date-dependent specs
gitCommit.body:
Batch the backfill, and unbomb two date-dependent specs

Review follow-ups on the backfill path:

- The rake preview looked up both category names per printed row. One
  pluck per user replaces 2N queries.
- Backfiller loaded every statement transaction the user has ever had,
  plus a parallel array of match candidates. It now runs in batches of
  500 and sorts the (much smaller) change list by date afterwards, since
  in_batches orders by primary key.
- The write goes through @user.transactions rather than Transaction, so
  the user scope is enforced at the write instead of inferred.

Two specs also started failing once this branch was rebased onto #319,
which added the opening_balance_date gate to auto-linking:

- backfiller_spec's debt-relink example could never link: the debt
  factory defaults opening_balance_date to CURRENT_DATE and the
  transaction factory dates rows in 2025.
- saving_spec:335 is a date bomb on main, not a bug here. target_date is
  Date.current + 364 — exactly 52 weeks and 26 fortnights, but the
  monthly count is calendar months crossed, so from the 1st of a month it
  lands on the 31st before the anniversary and counts 11. Pinning the
  clock to a 2nd makes all four frequencies exact.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
